title: How to Deal With Iran
gist: Five months into a U.S./Israel–Iran war that has closed the Strait of Hormuz, Jukic argues Iran's commoditized drone and missile industrial base — not maritime law — is the binding constraint, so no military option reopens the strait in time; the only depression-avoiding path is an 'economic relief for bombing restraint' deal that formalizes partial Iranian control of the strait, while the West spends 5–10 years reindustrializing, rearming with cheap interceptor drones, and diversifying energy to erode Iran's edge.

insights.claim: Oil and natural gas supply 58 percent of all global energy consumption, and the Persian Gulf region produces 31 percent of world crude and 18 percent of world natural gas while accounting for 42 percent of global oil exports and 27 percent of global LNG exports, making a sustained Hormuz closure a systemic rather than regional shock.
insights.speaker: Marko Jukic
insights.so_what: Sizes the tail risk: energy and shipping exposure should be priced off a multi-quarter Gulf export disruption, not a headline-driven spike.
